source_text: I. Et nobis est apud vos certamen, dilectissimi fratres, ut nihil aliud agendum dei servis et Christo eius dicatis, quam de multitudine fratrum cogitare; qua vi, qua ratione hic amor, hoc officium ad has nos impulit litteras, ut fratribus post futuris et magnificentiae dei fidele testimonium et labores ac tolerantiam nostri pro domino memoriae relinqueremus. II. Post popularem tumultum quem ferox vultus praesidis in necem concitavit, postque sequentis diei acerrimam persecutionem Christianorum, praevaricata violentia apprehensi sumus Lucius Montanus Flavianus Iulianus Victoricus Primolus Renus et Donatianus catecuminus, qui baptizatus in carcere statim spiritum reddidit, ab aquae baptismo ad martyrii coronam immaculato itinere festinans. nec non et circa Primolum similis consummationis exitus contigit; nam et ipsum ante paucos menses habita confessio baptizavit.
thought_title: Why the prisoners write to later brothers
orientation: The imprisoned confessors open their prison letter to fellow Christians to explain why they are writing.
pass_a_gloss: And there is for us before you a struggle, most beloved brothers, that you should say that nothing else must be done by servants of God and of his Christ, than to be thinking about the multitude of the brothers; with what force, with what account this love, this duty drove us to these letters, that for brothers who will be afterwards we might leave behind for remembrance both faithful testimony of the magnificence of God and our labors and endurance for the Lord. After the tumult of the people which the fierce face of the governor stirred up unto killing, and after the most sharp persecution of Christians of the following day, with violence that had turned aside we were arrested, Lucius Montanus Flavian Julian Victoricus Primolus Renus and Donatianus a person preparing for baptism, who baptized in prison immediately gave back his spirit, hastening from baptism of water to crown of martyrdom by an unstained journey. And also in the case of Primolus a like outcome of completion happened; for also the testimony held a few months before baptized him.

pass_b_english: Dearest brothers, our struggle lies before you, so that you say the servants of God and his Christ have nothing else to do but think of the multitude of the brothers. That love and that duty have driven us, by their own force and reason, to write this letter, so that for the brothers who come after us we may leave a faithful testimony to the greatness of God and a remembrance of our labors and our endurance for the Lord.

After the mob uproar that the governor's fierce face stirred toward killing, and after the bitter persecution of Christians on the following day, crooked violence seized us: Lucius, Montanus, Flavian, Julian, Victoricus, Primolus, Renus, and Donatian, a person preparing for baptism. Baptized in prison, Donatian immediately gave up his spirit, hastening by an unstained path from the baptism of water to the crown of martyrdom. A like completion met Primolus as well, for the testimony he had given a few months earlier had baptized him.
notes: List reads Primolum in accusative form among nominative names; glossed as the person Primolus; sense is arrest of Primolus. No damage marked in this section; no text invented.

problems.quote: we ask you to set apart the servants of God and his Christ for nothing else but care for the multitude of the brothers
problems.source_quote: ut nihil aliud agendum dei servis et Christo eius dicatis, quam de multitudine fratrum cogitare
problems.why: 'dicatis' is 'you say/declare' (subjunctive), not 'set apart'. Sense: you say the servants of God and Christ have nothing else to do but think of the brothers. Also 'ut' clause is misrendered.
problems.fix: Our struggle is shared with you, dearest brothers, so that you say the servants of God and of his Christ have nothing else to do but think of the multitude of the brothers.
problems.ruling: dicatis is from dicere 'say', not dicare 'dedicate'; set apart changes meaning

edits.old: and we ask you to set apart the servants of God and his Christ for nothing else but care for the multitude of the brothers
edits.new: so that you say the servants of God and his Christ have nothing else to do but think of the multitude of the brothers

fixed: Fixed dicatis-clause as 'you say': source has ut ... dicatis ... quam de multitudine fratrum cogitare with dei servis et Christo eius, i.e. you say the servants have nothing else to do but think of the brothers, not 'set apart'.
